1.pericope_label: Eliphaz bids Job call on the saints, and traces the prosperity of the fool to its curse

debates.question: Who are the saints, or holy ones, to whom Job is bidden turn?

sides.position: godly men, whose unanimous verdict Eliphaz claims for himself
the angels, as in Psalm 89, to whom no cry can avail
creatures as dependent on divine support as Job himself, able to do nothing but as God directs

debates.question: Whose wrath is it that kills the foolish man?

sides.position: any of three: God's revealed wrath, the man's own fatal passion, or the acts his rage drives him to
the man's own, Job injuring himself by quarrelling with God and envying his friends
God's, as a maxim: wrath falls only on the impious, so Job must be impious

debates.question: What is the last word of the fifth verse?

sides.position: the thirsty rather than the robber, since what follows is swallowing
perhaps a trap or a snare, though old versions read the thirsty and complete the parallel
an intriguer, snatching after the wealth

outliers: Henry alone separates foresight from desire, insisting Eliphaz did not pray for the ruin he foretold but prognosticated it.
Clarke alone spends his longest note on the starved desert banditti, citing Volney on legs of tendon without calf and six dates a day.
Ellicott alone reads the crushing in the gate as the children crushing one another, ruined by their own rivalries.
Clarke alone replaces the sparks with the sons of the coal lifting up their flight, bold men who rise above their trials.
themes: a question put as an appeal to arbitration
whether the holy ones are men or angels
prosperity conceded in order to be withdrawn
a tribunal sitting in the city gate
one contested word at the end of the fifth verse

6.pericope_label: Affliction does not spring from the ground: seek unto God, who catches the wise in their own craftiness

debates.question: Where does affliction come from, if not from the dust?

sides.position: from the will of God, prosperity and adversity not being proportioned as exactly as day and night
from God's justice, so that without an adequate cause Job could not be so afflicted
the word means iniquity as well as affliction, so Aben Ezra reads both clauses of moral evil

debates.question: Who disappoints the devices of the crafty?

sides.position: on a Jewish reading, the rain itself, defeating hoarders who must now sell cheap
God directly, in the baffling of Ahithophel, Sanballat and Haman, and in the universal proverb of the pit-digger
God, every attribute in the catalogue being chosen designedly to bring down haughtiness

debates.question: How is the sword from their mouth to be construed?

sides.position: the construction is harsh; eleven manuscripts read the sword of their mouth, with the Chaldee and Vulgate
a matter of grammatical nicety only, the point being God as the Saviour of those who have none

debates.question: What stops its mouth at the close of the passage?

sides.position: folly
iniquity, that is, wicked men silenced while the poor man hopes for the seventh deliverance

outliers: Henry alone undercuts the advice he reports, remarking that it is easy to say what we would do in another case and the trial often proves it not so easy.
Ellicott alone suspects the daytime darkness of alluding to the Egyptian plague that might be felt, and calls it a possible note of date.
Wesley alone finds the wonder of rain in a heavy body hung in the air and distributed as God sees fit.
Ellicott alone notes that froward means crooked, the name Naphtali deriving from the same root.
themes: trouble as the estate man is born to
a counsel transferred to the speaker himself
rain named because its commonness makes men reckon it little
the crafty taken in their own snare
the Saviour of those who have no saviour

17.pericope_label: Happy is the man whom God correcteth: the seven deliverances, the league with the stones, and the ripe grave

debates.question: What makes the blessing on correction true?

sides.position: only the hope of everlasting blessedness, which shows what the ancients already held
that correction mortifies corruption and weans the heart, so a man is happy because he is afflicted
the argument of Hebrews, that the Father of spirits corrects in order to impart his holiness

debates.question: What is the league with the stones of the field?

sides.position: the stones themselves, harmless to the barefoot, fruitful even as stony ground, and useful as boundary marks
strongholds where banditti and chiefs kept, so that the promise is confederacy instead of raids
a bold metaphor: a covenant with God is a covenant with all the creatures

debates.question: Does the twenty-fourth verse promise not sinning?

sides.position: no: the word means to miss the mark, so the promise is to visit the dwelling and miss nothing
the tabernacle at least is literal, a tent such as eastern houses were, neither Moses’s nor the suffering body

outliers: Ellicott alone turns on the whole passage, calling it a beautiful picture of the security of faith vitiated by its want of correspondence with facts, of which Job's own case was the crucial instance.
Ellicott alone objects to the boastful confidence of the close, Eliphaz speaking as though Job’s experience were nothing beside his own.
Delitzsch alone works the philology of the ripe age, an Arabic verb for being shrivelled with age matched by sheaves carried to the threshing-floor at harvest’s end.
Clarke alone reports the Chaldee reading of the whole chapter as Israel in Egypt, the famine Egypt’s, the war Amalek’s and the tongue Balaam’s incantation.
themes: a word for happy found nowhere else in this book
the hand that wounds applying the cure
a promise to miss nothing rather than not to sin
a speech that is answered by the case it was meant to fit
